narrative.overview:
Cream paper, forest controls and rounded Nunito lettering frame a detailed honey-timber illustration. The room carries the material richness: sunlit wood, checked fabric, foliage, a patterned rug, framed pictures and an empty side bed. Earned objects have illustrated silhouettes and consistent timber bases. Original Pokémon sprites remain independent of this artwork.

This is a local record of the shipped static sheets in `docs/design-v2/final`, not a replacement for the application theme or older design directions. Its evidence is the generated `index.html`, its `build.py`, the canonical asset manifest/proof, inspected master/first-tier-room/open-album/locked-album PNGs, and the product constraints in root `PRODUCT.md` and `DECOR.md`, `SHOP.md`, `ACHIEVEMENTS.md`. The direction contract lands as a fixed detailed companion room with independent awards; the original three sheets show visiting the pet, 12 shop entries and the 26-card album with three shelf selections. The five-section navigation precedes the wide room; three care bars and care actions follow it. The form is a static Operate sheet, seed `pokecorner-fixed-room`.

CSS dimensions below are source-derived, not browser-computed measurements. Artwork appearance was inspected in PNGs; manifest coordinates are intrinsic asset measurements. `QA.md` says `ship` for art exports and code/spec consistency only. It does not establish live CSS rendering, responsive acceptance, font loading, GIF playback, WPF behavior or user visual approval. Buttons are disabled, navigation sections are spans, balances/progress are demonstration values and there is no runtime JavaScript.

User follow-up 2026-10-11: one corner album entry, shelf selection inside the album, twelve transparent shop icons. TROPHY-SEMANTICS.md documented three card families for replacement and six for refinement; those proposals were approved and completed as detailed below. User review of the resulting new pictures remains open.

User-approved semantic corrections completed: 20 newly generated trophies plus 4 original population stages restored. Updated canonical colors, exact-alpha masks, room/album previews and 168 placements. Current sources/accepted prompts are in trophy-revision/jobs.json; game IDs and conditions remain unchanged.

The extension ships settings, six short onboarding steps and eighteen service states in the same Nunito/paper/forest grammar. They are static declarations and do not confirm browser layout or runtime behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Detailed fixed interior with independently positioned earned objects.
Cream surfaces, forest actions and descriptive Nunito text.
Plain divided catalog rows instead of boxed cards within boxed cards.
Exact-alpha locked silhouettes that preserve first-tier secrecy.

rules.name: The Material Carries Color Rule
rules.body: Keep the room and awards in their source raster colors; use the extracted paper and forest palette for the surrounding controls.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Use Nunito for titles, descriptions, navigation and controls; preserve the source's size-based hierarchy without introducing a separate display face.

rules.name: The Shared Coordinate Frame Rule
rules.body: Register room, awards, shelf lip and independent pet against the same 1448×582 scene, then scale the composition together.

rules.name: The Shelf Occlusion Rule
rules.body: Draw the clean room first, independent awards second, the intrinsic shelf lip third, and the independent pet above the scene layers.

rules.name: The Earned Appearance Rule
rules.body: Show the last earned chain appearance; before the first award, use only the first-tier exact-alpha silhouette, never a later-tier preview.

dos: Do retain the source room's timber, fabric, foliage and illustrated depth while keeping controls on cream paper.
Do scale the room and independent layers in one coordinate frame and position awards by their recorded feet.
Do show one album entry per chain and preserve the first-tier locked silhouette until its first award.
Do use Nunito, descriptive status text and the repeated forest/paper control treatments.
Do keep game assets, archived sources and review previews distinct when handing off the scene.
donts: Don't bake the pet or earned awards into the master room or draw awards above the shelf-front lip.
Don't expose future chain-tier art through a locked card or place locked awards on the shelf.
Don't promote archived customization IDs or the eight preview PNGs into the active asset inventory.
Don't treat static demo balances, disabled controls or CSS declarations as proof of gameplay, live rendering or user acceptance.
